<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/temporal-comparand-door.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/analytics.mdx`  _(via current_iso_week (symbol, a field of const object PERIOD_KEY_RESOLVERS; a field of const object PERIOD_KEY_TOKEN_DESCRIPTIONS), current_iso_week (literal, a string literal in PERIOD_KEY_TOKENS; a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-view.mdx`  _(via current_iso_week (symbol, a field of const object PERIOD_KEY_RESOLVERS; a field of const object PERIOD_KEY_TOKEN_DESCRIPTIONS), current_iso_week (literal, a string literal in PERIOD_KEY_TOKENS; a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/ui/dashboards.mdx`  _(via current_iso_week (symbol, a field of const object PERIOD_KEY_RESOLVERS; a field of const object PERIOD_KEY_TOKEN_DESCRIPTIONS), current_iso_week (literal, a string literal in PERIOD_KEY_TOKENS; a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via GlobalFilterSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/temporal-comparand-door.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **183** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a1b14cdff8df4a203af978290c65c357f1b565c5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `215425cea8b544837cb83e55259b9949927ecfc0` — the merge of head `3c0e95c7e4f30f7b3fd92e1162ebabd957416672` into base `a1b14cdff8df4a203af978290c65c357f1b565c5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 215425cea8b544837cb83e55259b9949927ecfc0 && git checkout 215425cea8b544837cb83e55259b9949927ecfc0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a1b14cdff8df4a203af978290c65c357f1b565c5 3c0e95c7e4f30f7b3fd92e1162ebabd957416672 && git checkout -B drift-repro a1b14cdff8df4a203af978290c65c357f1b565c5 && git merge --no-ff 3c0e95c7e4f30f7b3fd92e1162ebabd957416672

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a1b14cdff8df4a203af978290c65c357f1b565c5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a1b14cdff8df4a203af978290c65c357f1b565c5` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：仪表盘上按“周”筛选的文本条件，默认值可以写成一个“本周”占位符，每次打开都会自动显示当前周（比如 2026-W47），不用每周手改。
- 为什么做：以前只能写死某一周，过了周一就过时了。
- 出错会怎样：只是多认一个占位符；以前写的筛选条件和默认值照旧生效。日期类筛选不接受这个占位符，避免把“周编号”当成日期用错。
- 要你做什么：不需要你做任何事。它给元数据加了一个新写法，席位会安排一次约定审核，然后由区域落地。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT (L1-a) · repo:objectstack#5 · head `fa840834a0fa7bab6b99484992acee7896f660e4` · 2026-11-19T08:27Z

- **形态** — 26 files, +737/−39 (776 lines, 46 of them generated), spread across the packages below. Base `c05a8a01`, K=10. `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 35391`: not governed, under the 3000-line limit. `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`. Levels: `spec` minor, the other three patch, which is right for the kind.
  - `spec`: `date-macros.zod.ts`, `context-tokens.zod.ts`, `dashboard.zod.ts`, and the `api-surface` / `export-origins` ledgers.
  - `core`: the server resolver.
  - `lint`.
  - `@object-ui/core`: the client resolver and dashboard defaults.
  - five docs pages, tests, and one changeset.
- **Fixes vs card #34938, per maintainer ruling B (record 7000277555)**
  - **One token, in its own list.** `PERIOD_KEY_TOKENS = ['current_iso_week']` is a separate closed list, never spread into `DATE_MACRO_TOKENS`. So `isDateMacroToken` is false for it, and the date-only surfaces still refuse it: a `type: 'date'` default, `isDateMacroPlaceholder`, and `calendar.initialDate`.
  - **Known filter token.** `isKnownFilterToken` admits it, and `classifyFilterToken` answers a new kind, `period-key`. Lint, flow operands and the server resolver all read those two predicates.
  - **Server resolution.** `PERIOD_KEY_RESOLVERS` uses `bucketDateKey(now, 'week', ctx.timezone)`, the analytics week label. The table is exhaustive by `satisfies Record<PeriodKeyToken, …>`.
  - **Client resolution.**
    - `resolvePeriodKeyTokens` matches the whole value only; `'week {current_iso_week}'` is left as written.
    - It walks plain objects and arrays.
    - `isoWeekKey` computes the Thursday-of-week rule and the ISO year by the standard algorithm.
    - It runs in `resolveFilterPlaceholders` after the date macros.
    - The dashboard defaults resolve it for every filter type except `date` / `dateRange`.
  - **Parity.** One 16-row parity table (the year edges and four time zones) runs on both sides.
  - **The error text** of `UnknownFilterTokenError` now lists the token.
  - **Not widened.** A near spelling (`{currentIsoWeek}`) is still refused as unknown.
- **Changeset** — read sentence by sentence against the diff, and all of it matches:
  - the stale-week motive and the example;
  - the `YYYY-Www` rule with its two year-edge examples (2027-01-01 → `2026-W53`, 2025-12-29 → `2026-W01`);
  - the workspace time zone;
  - the separate list, and the date default and `initialDate` refusals;
  - the new `period-key` kind;
  - where it resolves on the server and on the client;
  - a literal key stays fixed;
  - whole-value only, and the near spelling still refused;
  - the warning against using it on date columns.
- **Pins** — the core and `@object-ui/core` resolver suites (including the parity table and year edges); `context-tokens` / `date-macros` classification and the date-macro exclusion; dashboard schema and filter defaults (text resolves, date refuses, literal stays fixed); and lint's acceptance of the token.
- **Ablation: NOT MEASURED** (os-dev report 7003178228). On base the token answered `FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN` 400, so each resolve pin is red on base by construction, but no pin was mutated and re-run. Accepted for a pure addition, where the base cannot pass the new pins. Recorded as not measured.
- **门禁** — 74 check-runs on this head: 63 success, 11 skipped, 0 failure.
- **接受的偏差** — fence extensions named in the PR's Acceptance notes: `lint/rule-explanations.ts` (the explanation text), the client `filter-tokens.ts` (the one-call entry point every surface uses), and two docs pages. Each is needed for the token to be known or documented where the ruling places it. Accepted.
- **范围外去向** — already filed on the seat's word: #35394 (p2, temporal-comparand step-around, pre-existing), #35395 (p3, compare-to, blocked by this PR), #35396 (p3, lint over text defaults). The `skills` `filters.md` follow-up is the seat's after merge, since that path is governed.
- **L2 owed (routing)** — `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and non-test `packages/spec/src/**` → contract review at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER. Routed to seat 5.
- **落地条款** — not governed. ux-1 lands after the seat's L2 record. A new push needs a fresh L1 only if it changes more than a main merge.

repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CbUb7TcZK1XUAddUmQ

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fa840834a0fa7bab6b99484992acee7896f660e4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/context-tokens.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/date-macros.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.zod.ts + packages/core/src/utils/filter-tokens.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-filter-tokens.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, ui/packages/core/src/utils/date-macros.ts, ui/packages/core/src/utils/dashboard-filters.ts, ui/packages/core/src/utils/filter-tokens.ts

Inputs read: card #34938 (body, triage, ruling record 7000277555, claim 7001845808, os-dev report 7003178228), PR #35391 (body, file list, net diff against the merge base, comments 7003161269 / 7003787253 / 7003847515), and the 74 check-runs on the head: 63 success, 11 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Ruling B, "add one fixed placeholder" — held.** `PERIOD_KEY_TOKENS` is a closed `as const` list with exactly one member, `current_iso_week`. No parameterised grammar, no expression default, no last/next-week member, no new filter control, no schema key. `GlobalFilterSchema.defaultValue` keeps its type (`string | number | boolean`); only its TSDoc and `describe` text change. A list, a predicate, a description table and a resolver table for one word is the same shape `RECORD_CONTEXT_TOKENS` took for one word; it is a closed vocabulary, not a general mechanism. Right.
- **Accept-set, filter values: widened by one spelling (two with `${…}`).** `isKnownFilterToken('current_iso_week')` goes `false` → `true`; `classifyFilterToken('{current_iso_week}')` goes `unknown` → `period-key`. Every reader follows from those two: lint `filter-token-unknown` stops flagging it, the flow CRUD filter operand (`classifyFlowFilterOperandString`, not in the diff) reads it as `placeholder`, and the server resolver resolves it instead of answering `FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN` / 400. All three are inside the ruling's "usable in any filter condition". Right.
- **Accept-set, date-only surfaces: unchanged.** `isDateMacroToken`, `DATE_MACRO_TOKENS`, `DATE_MACRO_WRAPPED_RE` and `checkGlobalFilterDateDefaultValue` are untouched, so a `type: 'date'` default and `calendar.initialDate` still refuse the token. Right, and it is the reason the sibling list is the correct design.
- **Public surface: four new `@objectstack/spec/data` exports** (`PERIOD_KEY_TOKENS`, `PeriodKeyToken`, `isPeriodKeyToken`, `PERIOD_KEY_TOKEN_DESCRIPTIONS`), in both generated ledgers; one new `@object-ui/core` export (`resolvePeriodKeyTokens`, through `export * from './utils/date-macros.js'`). Additive. Right.
- **Return union of `classifyFilterToken` gains `{ kind: 'period-key' }` — ruled explicitly.** It is a widening of what the function can answer. At run time nothing that was accepted is refused. At compile time, a consumer that switches exhaustively on `kind` with a `never` check stops compiling until it handles the new kind. That is the cost of every added union member, and this repo has ruled on the identical case: the `record-context` kind was added in a minor (17.5.0, changeset `e7f69db`), with the sentence "A consumer that switches exhaustively on `kind` gets a compile error until it handles the new kind." So: widening, minor, not a major. All twelve in-tree call sites were read; none switches exhaustively. Each either tests `!== null`, or tests one kind by name (`unknown`, `record-context`, `date-macro`). The one behaviour that follows for a "one kind by name" reader is `judgeResolvedToken` in objectql, which judges `date-macro` only and therefore leaves a period key unjudged: see S1.
- **Temporal-comparand door: this PR does add the new token to the #35394 class.** On base, `{current_iso_week}` against a `date` / `datetime` / `time` column answered `FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN` / 400. On this head it answers 200: `isUninterpretableTemporalComparand` (core `temporal-comparand.ts`) steps around every string `classifyFilterToken` knows, the resolver turns it into `2026-W47`, and `judgeResolvedToken` skips it. The dev measured `$lt` returning every row and `$eq` / `$gte` returning none, while the literal `'2026-W47'` on the same column is refused `INVALID_FILTER` / 400. The class pre-exists for `{current_user_id}`; this change enrols a second, clock-shaped member in it. Wrong as it stands: S1.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `@objectstack/spec` minor; `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@object-ui/core` patch. The spec level is right: additive exports plus one added union member, matching the 17.5.0 precedent above. No narrowing, so no major. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening: the closed filter-placeholder vocabulary gains one token)` is present, identical, on the claim, the PR body and the changeset, and is the true reading of the diff. `Metadata-protocol: added` is right: one new authorable spelling, nothing removed or re-read.
- The changeset's body was read against the tree and each sentence holds, including both year-edge examples (2027-01-01 → `2026-W53`, 2025-12-29 → `2026-W01`). It omits one sentence the precedent carried: see N1.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Deviation 1, fence extensions (`rule-explanations.ts`, the client `filter-tokens.ts`, two docs pages): accepted. The first states a count the change made false; the second is the one entry point surfaces are told to call; both are in Scope above and reviewed in ④.
- Deviation 4, levels as dispatched: answered in ②.
- Deviation 6, `flow-value-slot-template.ts` docblock and the lint hint text left as written: N2 and N3.
- Out-of-scope: temporal-comparand step-around (#35394): NOT accepted as wholly out of scope for this token. See S1. The pre-existing context-token half stays #35394's.
- Out-of-scope: compare-to does not shift a period key (#35395): accepted as a follow-up. The comparison series filtering the same week is a missing feature on a new token, not a wrong answer on an existing one.
- Out-of-scope: lint does not walk `globalFilters[].defaultValue` (#35396): accepted as a follow-up. A typo there is refused at query time (400), so it is loud, only late.
- Skills follow-up (`skills/objectstack-query/rules/filters.md`), routed to the seat. It must say, in the "Date Macros" section: (a) `{current_iso_week}` (and `${current_iso_week}`) is a period key from `PERIOD_KEY_TOKENS` in `data/date-macros.zod.ts`, a sibling list, not a date macro; (b) it resolves to today's ISO-8601 week key `YYYY-Www` in the workspace time zone, Monday-start weeks, the ISO week-numbering year at the year edges (2027-01-01 is `2026-W53`); (c) the value is text: use it only on a text field that stores week keys, never on a `date` / `datetime` / `time` field, where `{current_week_start}` / `{current_week_end}` or the `this_week` preset is the spelling, and state what the door answers there once S1 is closed; (d) a `type: 'date'` dashboard default and `calendar.initialDate` refuse it, a text filter default accepts it and shows the resolved key; (e) whole value only; (f) in the "Scope" paragraph, the client resolver list gains `resolvePeriodKeyTokens()`, and `resolveFilterPlaceholders()` is the one call that covers all three vocabularies. No last/next-week token exists and the section must not imply one.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The token becomes a string literal before the query reaches a driver; no id is materialised and no join moves in-app.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/date-macros.zod.ts`** against the ruling and its first consumer (a `type: 'text'` global filter over `cost_week`). The list is closed, single-member and kept out of `DATE_MACRO_TOKENS`, and the module doc gives the reason (every reader of that list takes its members as dates). The stated rule (Monday start, week 1 holds the first Thursday, ISO week-numbering year, Friday 2027-01-01 = `2026-W53`, Monday 2027-01-04 = `2027-W01`) is ISO 8601 and was checked by hand. Holds.

**`packages/spec/src/data/context-tokens.zod.ts`.** `isKnownFilterToken` and `classifyFilterToken` agree with each other for the new token; the branch sits after `date-macro` and before the suggestion table, so a near spelling (`{currentIsoWeek}`) is still `unknown`. The docblock's reason for a separate kind is sound. Holds; the union ruling is in ①.

**`packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.zod.ts`.** Docs-only on `defaultValue`; the text matches what `resolveDashboardFilterDefs` does (every type except `date` / `dateRange` resolves; a date filter refuses). Holds.

**`packages/core/src/utils/filter-tokens.ts`** (server). `PERIOD_KEY_RESOLVERS` is exhaustive by `satisfies Record<PeriodKeyToken, …>` and delegates to `bucketDateKey(now, 'week', ctx.timezone)`. `isoWeekLabelFromCalendarDay` was read: it shifts to the week's Thursday, takes that Thursday's year as the ISO year and counts from January 4. It answers W53 for 2020 and 2026 and puts January 1–3 in the prior ISO year when they fall Friday to Sunday. The day is read through `calendarPartsInTzOrUtc`, so the zone is the request's, UTC when none is set, exactly as the date macros. One `now` is pinned for the whole tree. Agrees with the contract.

**`ui/packages/core/src/utils/date-macros.ts`** (client). `isoWeekKey` is the ordinal form of the same rule (Thursday of the week, then `floor(days since January 1 of the Thursday's year / 7) + 1`); checked by hand on 2025-12-29, 2026-11-19, 2026-12-31, 2027-01-01, 2027-01-03 and 2027-01-04, equal to the server on each. It builds days with `setUTCFullYear`, so no DST or two-digit-year drift. "Today" is `calendarDayIn(now, getDisplayTimeZone())`, the date macros' own reading. Whole-string match only, own-property lookup, plain objects only. With no zone declared the client reads the viewer's clock and the server reads UTC; that is the date macros' existing behaviour, inherited, not introduced. Agrees with the contract.

**`ui/packages/core/src/utils/dashboard-filters.ts` and `ui/packages/core/src/utils/filter-tokens.ts`.** The default is resolved before it seeds the filter variable, so the box shows the key; `date` / `dateRange` are left to their own normalizer; a literal key passes through. `resolveFilterPlaceholders` threads one `now` to both clock vocabularies. Agree.

**`packages/lint/src/validate-filter-tokens.ts` and `rule-explanations.ts`.** No logic change; the explanation's count is corrected to three. Agree, except N3.

Findings:

S1 (should-fix) — A period key must not be stepped around at the temporal-comparand door. This PR turns `{current_iso_week}` on a `date` / `datetime` / `time` column from `FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN` / 400 into a 200 that compares a week key against a date as text (`$lt`: every row; `$eq` / `$gte`: none), where the literal `'2026-W47'` is refused `INVALID_FILTER` / 400. The contract written in this diff says the value "is TEXT … a week key is not a date" and that date surfaces "refuse it"; the query door is the one date surface that does not, and the changeset documents the wrong answer instead of refusing it. A week token is the placeholder most likely to be written against a date column. Close it one of two ways: in this PR, have the door judge a `period-key` placeholder as written (it is not a calendar day, an instant or a wall-clock time, so it takes the literal's refusal), with a pin on a date, a datetime and a time column and a positive control on a text column; or land #35394 first with `period-key` named in its fix and its pins, then rebase. The context-token half of the class stays #35394's either way. The docs and changeset sentence "the key is compared as text, so the answer is wrong" then becomes "refused".

N1 (nit) — The changeset says `classifyFilterToken` "answers a new kind, `period-key`" but not what that costs a consumer. The precedent (`e7f69db`, 17.5.0) carried "A consumer that switches exhaustively on `kind` gets a compile error until it handles the new kind." Add the sentence; S1 moves the head anyway.

N2 (nit) — `packages/spec/src/automation/flow-value-slot-template.ts` (not in the diff) still describes a CRUD filter placeholder as "a context token or a date macro", while `isKnownFilterToken` now also admits period keys there. Follow-up card or the S1 commit.

N3 (nit) — The lint hint strings in `validate-filter-tokens.ts` still offer "a context token … or a date macro" and its inline comment says "the two vocabularies in full"; `os explain` now lists three. The remedy line is still correct for a typo, so no effect on correctness.

No must-fix. One should-fix, S1, open on this head: the record does not clear the PR to land until a delta review closes it.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-34938-current-iso-week-token`
